POTENTIAL PROBLEMS
The potential problems which may be encountered on this project involve the following:
1.) Unit #7  This family consists of the mother as head of the household; a son (age 10); and two daughters (7 and 2 years of age). The family is presently receiving aid through A.D.C. pending the results and final decree in a divorce suit filed against the husband. The uncertainty at this time regarding this family's recurring income in the future is actually the item of potential difficulty. Until the divorce proceedings are completed, we cannot determine their annual income and consequently cannot determine the amount they can afford to pay.
2.) Unit #10  This family consists of a divorced woman as head of the household; her three children- (a girl  age 13; and boys  ages 21 and 4); and the divorced grandmother. The only admitted income is derived in the form of A.D.C. received by the head of the household. The grandmother would not discuss her finances or income, if any, nor would the oldest son. We were told that no one in the family worked, yet they pay $125 per month for rent and requested replacement housing for a like rental. As a matter of fact, they talked about purchasing a home probably under the Section 235 program.
The apparent solution to this and the previous case will be to begin working with these families as soon as authorization is obtained in the hope of finding out the truth regarding their total income and exact family situations and the level of any substantial recurring income. Another concern will be the availability and adequacy of public transportation which will very likely be their primary mode of transportation.
A sincere and concentrated effort will be necessary to provide solutions for these two family groups.
